transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I came in because I keep hearing these voices. They are as clear as somebody standing right there in my little studio, just saying my name and telling me my work is being judged. And I don't know why they'd say that, because I work real hard. I'm a personal care aide, you know? I take care of folks who can't do for themselves. Just yesterday I was over at Mr. Miller's place, helping him with his meals. He likes his soup piping hot, burns his tongue half the time, but he won't eat it if it's even a little cold. I always have to use that old microwave of his that smells like burnt popcorn. I told his daughter she needs to buy him a new one, but she never listens to me. But... yeah, even when I go home and my house is completely quiet, and nobody is there with me... I still hear them. Just judging my work.
About how long have you been hearing these voices?

It's been... I'd say about nine months now. Nine months of the voices, and just this... this constant, fixed fear I have that my work is being watched all the time. 

I know it was nine months ago because it started right around the time I bought my new work shoes. They're these thick, white non-slip ones. You really gotta have good shoes when you're lifting folks, plus the linoleum floors over at Mrs. Gable's house—she's another client of mine—they get so slippery if you spill even a drop of water. It's like an ice rink in her kitchen. My cousin slipped at her job at the grocery store and messed up her knee so bad she was stuck on the couch for a whole year. She just sat there watching those daytime judge shows, eating those little square orange cheese crackers. I can't stand those crackers, they get all gummy in your teeth and turn your fingers completely orange, like you painted them. 

But I couldn't just sit around like her, you know? I have to keep working, I have bills. I'm a hard worker. But... yeah, nine months of them watching me and saying those things.
During these past nine months, have you experienced periods of feeling deeply down, depressed, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Depressed? No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really get down like that, I don't have the time to sit around moping. I still like doing my usual things. Like my knitting... I knit these little square blankets for the premature babies down at the hospital. You have to use the softest yarn, 100% acrylic, because you can't use wool on those little babies. 

Wool makes me itch so bad anyway. I bought this wool sweater at a thrift store a few years back, a really pretty blue one, kind of like a robin's egg? But I wore it to church and I was scratching my neck the entire sermon. Reverend Thomas kept looking right at me from the pulpit, he probably thought I had a rash or fleas or something. He always gives these really long sermons, mostly from the Old Testament. I don't know why he likes it so much, it's just a bunch of rules about what you can and can't eat. I love a good pork chop, so I just tune that part out. You gotta fry them in a cast iron skillet with a little bit of bacon grease to get that good crust on the outside. If you use a regular non-stick pan, they just get gray and rubbery. 

But no, I haven't been sad or lost interest in anything. Just... just hearing them judge me.
Do you use any recreational drugs, or drink alcohol?

No, I don't touch any of that stuff. Drugs and alcohol, they just mess with your head and your body. I've seen it enough with some of the folks in my neighborhood. There's this one man, Mr. Henderson, lives a few doors down from me. He sits on his porch all day drinking those tall cans of beer in the brown paper bags. He leaves the empty cans all over his front lawn, and when the wind picks up, they blow right into my flower beds. I have these beautiful petunias I planted in the spring. You have to water them every single morning before the sun gets too hot, otherwise the leaves get all crispy and brown. I use this little green watering can I got at the hardware store. It has a little spout that sprinkles the water real gentle, like rain. If you use a hose, it just blasts the dirt right out of the pot and makes a huge muddy mess on the sidewalk. And then you track it into the house... and I tell you, getting mud out of a white rug is impossible. I tried that foam spray stuff once, but it just left a big yellow stain that looked worse than the mud. So I had to put a coffee table over it to hide it. It's a nice table, though, real oak. Heavy as a car. But no, I don't drink or do drugs. Never have.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any serious medical conditions or experienced a head injury?

No, no serious medical conditions. And I haven't hit my head or anything like that. I did bump my elbow pretty hard on the doorframe last week, right on the funny bone. It's not really funny at all, is it? It sends this horrible shooting pain all the way down to your pinky finger. I was carrying a load of laundry down to the basement when I did it. I have to do laundry twice a week because my work uniforms get so soiled. I wear these light blue scrubs, and every little stain shows up on them. Just the other day, I spilled a bit of tomato soup on my top while I was feeding Mr. Peterson. He's another client, a sweet older gentleman, but his hands shake terribly. It's a shame, really, because he used to be a watchmaker. Imagine that, working with all those tiny little gears and springs, and now he can barely hold a spoon. He showed me this pocket watch he made back in the seventies, gold plated with Roman numerals. I prefer digital watches myself, they're just easier to read when you're in a hurry. But no, my health is fine, no head injuries or anything.
